title: Together in practice
hookLine: an old couple asks the Buddha to meet again in the next life; his answer, and a week of family looked back on
tomorrow: and when love ends in a goodbye, what does kindness look like?

cards: Can an old couple meet again in the next life? Two of the Buddha's lay followers asked him exactly that. They're known by their son's name: Nakula's father and Nakula's mother.

He speaks first. She was brought to my home when we were both young, and in all the years since, I don't recall wronging her, not even in thought. We want to see each other in this life, and in the next.
Then she says the same, almost word for word.

teach.b: If two people want to meet in this life and the next, let them be matched: the same faith, saddha, the same virtue, the same generosity, the same wisdom. Then they will.

Notice what he doesn't say: be the same personality, want the same things, never disagree. He names four qualities to grow side by side. And he doesn't scold them for wanting more time, or call their wish clinging.
He takes an old couple's love seriously, and tells them what feeds it. Faith keeps them facing the same way. Virtue keeps them trustworthy to each other.
Generosity keeps their hands open. Wisdom keeps them seeing clearly, even as they change. This couple shared one path.
Some readers in families of two traditions hear the sutta as asking for that match in trust, goodness, giving and wisdom, practiced together.
And that's where the week ends up. Repair quickly: see the fault, make amends, hold back after. East: parents, with duties running both ways.
Hard to repay: goodness shared is the coin that counts. Kind and clear: a warm hand and steady feet. West: partners guarding one house from both sides.
Not owning: metta, an open hand.
Together is where all six lead: two people growing the same good things, side by side, for as long as they get.

how: Some Buddhist couples chant, meditate or visit the temple together, and some wedding blessings recall Nakula's parents as a picture of a couple matched in faith, virtue, generosity and wisdom.

o: two people growing the same good qualities side by side
two lives tied together by fate, no matter what
a monk and a nun who share one monastery

games.q: Nakula's parents, and a week of family — tap the pairs.
p: never wronged her, not even in thought
matched in faith, virtue, giving, wisdom
a warm hand and steady feet

s: the Buddha told Nakula's parents that wishing to stay together is clinging
he told them how: be matched in faith, virtue, generosity and wisdom, and they will see each other.
in the sutta, Nakula's mother says the same thing her husband said
both say they never wronged each other, even in thought, and want to meet in this life and the next.
the Buddha's condition was that the couple have the same personality
he named four qualities to grow together, not a matching personality.

games.q: you're Nakula's mother. you and your husband have asked the Buddha to meet again in the next life. he tells you how. what do you expect him to name?
o: four qualities to share: faith, virtue, generosity and wisdom.
a vow to marry no one else, sworn before the monks.
a large gift to the monastery, made in both your names.
games.why: the Buddha says: if both are matched in faith, virtue, generosity and wisdom, they will see each other in this life and the next.

practice: If someone you share a life with is nearby, sit these two minutes side by side, no talking, just breathing in the same room. If you're alone, bring one person to mind and sit as though they were beside you.
Let your breathing settle next to theirs. Nothing to fix, nothing to say; just two lives in one room for a little while.

wordCard.voice: Together in practice: two people matched in faith, virtue, generosity and wisdom, the Buddha's answer to Nakula's parents, who wanted one more life side by side.

orig.note: Pali: living alike, matched in life; the sutta's word for Nakula's parents.

carryVoice: Keep this one: together, growing the same good things side by side. Six of eleven, and the week is closed.

sources.ref: Anguttara Nikaya 4.55 (Samajivi Sutta: Nakula's father and Nakula's mother each say they have not transgressed against the other even in thought since she was brought to his home when both were young, and wish to see each other in this life and the next; the Buddha: if both have the same faith, virtue, generosity and wisdom, they will)
